name: Oz
def: Small electric tool carrier that weeds, sows and marks rows in market garden beds, driving itself between crop rows using satellite guidance.
body: Oz is the smallest of Naio's field robots, a compact electric platform that straddles or runs between narrow vegetable beds. It follows rows autonomously using corrected satellite positioning and carries a wide catalogue of interchangeable tools for weeding, sowing and row marking. It can also tow a small trailer or crates around a holding. Market gardeners and specialty crop growers in France and neighbouring countries use it on small intensive plots.
facts: More than 35 compatible implements are offered for weeding, sowing and row marking
Naio also builds the larger Dino for vegetable beds and Ted for vineyards
Aimed at market gardening and aromatic plant growers working small plots
specs: Four wheeled electric drive tool carrier with a maximum working width of one metre
Lithium battery giving up to eight hours of work
Autonomous row work guided by corrected satellite positioning, with obstacle detection and emergency stop
